subject: Request: short-term runtime exemption for session-migration (SolacePay), next steps
messages:
From: Sara Bloom <sara@solacepay.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: production session-migration anomalies

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for yesterday's walkthrough. We started a phased migration of our session tokens to the new SDK runtime this morning and are seeing intermittent 502-like resets when our client rotates tokens (roughly 1 in 3k requests). The failures look like short lived socket resets, then the client retries and succeeds.

This is blocking our final rollout—can your team confirm whether there are any known token-rotation edge cases in the new runtime? If there is a quick mitigation (routing to the previous variant or a flag we can enable), we may be able to finish our migration this week.

I've attached a small trace from our QA run.

Thanks,
Sara Bloom
Head of Platform
SolacePay Inc.
[attachment: demo-trace.zip (log archive)]

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Sara Bloom <sara@solacepay.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: production session-migration anomalies

Sara — thanks for the trace and for flagging this quickly.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- I looped in Karthik (runtime) and Logan (platform ops) to investigate root cause and propose a short-term mitigation.
- Can you confirm: token rotation frequency, client retry/backoff behavior, and whether the failures always include a TLS handshake reset?

Karthik — attaching the trace Sara sent. From my read: resets coincide with token swap windows and follow a single failed token-validate call. If we can provide a temporary route to the prior runtime variant for their tenant or enable a short-lived non-strict token fallback, they can finish rollout without reverting.

Proposed customer-facing plan (if you agree):
1) Immediate: enable tenant-level route to runtime-v1 for 48h while we collect detailed traces.
2) Short-term: push a hotfix or gate in runtime-v2 that tolerates in-flight token rotations for 72h.
3) Long-term: add a token-rotation test case to the nightly e2e harness and include a config knob for graceful token-swap behavior.

Sara — happy to jump on a quick call with you and Karthik/Logan if that helps. ETA from our side: first pass diagnosis within 4 hours.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Bloom <sara@solacepay.com>
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2028 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: production session-migration anomalies

On Tue, Jun 26, 2028 at 10:03 AM grace_oconnor@redwood.com wrote:
> Karthik — attaching the trace Sara sent. From my read: resets coincide with token swap windows and follow a single failed token-validate call. If we can provide a temporary route to the prior runtime variant for their tenant or enable a short-lived non-strict token fallback, they can finish rollout without reverting.

Thanks Grace — I dug into the trace and a couple internal logs. Short summary:
- Symptom: session channel is being torn down during KV cache refresh triggered by token rotate; the runtime is aggressively closing idle websocket frames when it detects an auth mismatch.
- Repro: I can reproduce locally with their token-rotation pattern (rotate every 60s, immediate retry). I attach repro steps below.

Repro steps (local):
1) Start client with token A.
2) After 45s, simulate rotation to token B and immediately perform 3 concurrent requests with no backoff.
3) Observe connection reset from runtime-v2 in ~1.2s, followed by client retry success.

Root cause hypothesis: a new strict auth check introduced in runtime-v2 invalidates in-flight requests during token swap when KV cache hasn't updated. We added the check to reduce replay risk, but it is too aggressive for clients that retry without exponential backoff.

Mitigation options (tradeoffs):
A) Tenant-level routing to runtime-v1 (no strict check). Low-risk externally, quick to enable. Requires platform ops to flip route.
B) Short-term hotfix: add a 200ms grace window in runtime-v2 around token-swap where stale cache entries are accepted. Medium-risk, requires MR and canary.
C) Customer-side: small client change (add 100ms jitter/backoff) — ideal long-term but blocks their immediate rollout.

I recommend A) for immediate rollout and B) as engineering follow-up. I opened an internal ticket SUP-321 and will push a canary for B if we get approval.

Attachments: internal log snippets pasted below and pointer to SUP-321.

-karthik
From: logan_wright@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Bloom <sara@solacepay.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Jun 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: production session-migration anomalies

Agree with Karthik's assessment. Operational note: tenant routing to runtime-v1 can be enabled per-tenant via the routing control plane; estimated impact: <5 minutes to flip and no downtime. Risk: customers on runtime-v1 won't get the new replay protections until we roll out the hotfix.

Grace — I drafted a short MOU for a temporary exemption (48h route to runtime-v1 + collection of traces + commitment to a hotfix timeline). Putting the draft here and attaching to the thread. If sales/legal are OK, we can send this to SolacePay and enable the routing immediately after their sign-off.

[attachment: draft-mou-solacepay.pdf]

Logan Wright
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Sara Bloom <sara@solacepay.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 28 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: production session-migration anomalies

Thanks everyone — plan sounds good. We've reviewed the MOU and Sara (ops) signed off internally. You have permission to flip the tenant route to runtime-v1 for the 48h window.

We'll add the minor 100ms jitter on our side next week, but we need the temporary routing to finish the migration now. If you can enable it after 18:00 PT today, that would work for us.

Also scheduling a 30-min sync for tomorrow so we can review traces and confirm rollback criteria.

—Sara
